span: The condition precedent for condonation of the delay in filing an application or appeal, is the existence of sufficient cause.
why: Holding: condonation is available only on sufficient cause (onus on the appellant), no formula; the delay is not condoned in this case.

span: it is not mandatory to file an application in writing before relief can be granted under the said section
why: Court reasons that s.5 empowers condonation even without a written application, while insisting that condonation cannot be claimed as of right.

span: whether the High Court was justified in not condoning the delay of 1942 days in filing the second appeal
why: States the question and the High Court's refusal; the Supreme Court's answer begins in the next paragraph.

span: Courts are empowered to exercise discretion to condone the delay if sufficient cause had been explained
why: Holding affirms the power but adds that it may be refused even where sufficient cause is shown (inordinate delay, negligence).

span: Not mandatory that written application be filed seeking condonation of delay and relief can be granted in that regard upon oral request, provided sufficient cause is shown for such delay
why: Concerns delay in filing a Change Report under a charity statute, not delay in filing an appeal.

span: High Court rightly refused to condone the delay
why: Holding: a 1788-day delay by the State was unexplained, so refusal to condone is upheld.

span: the application filed by the appellant for condonation of delay of 554 days in filing the appeal deserves to be condoned
why: Holding: illness was a sufficient cause and the delay is condoned.
